subject: Rights routing and training exclusion discussion — MSA & Order Form redlines
messages:
From: Elise Moreno <elise.moreno@novasys.io>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Becker <t.becker@novasys.io>, Novasys Legal <legal@novasys.io>
Date: 2029-01-12 09:14 -0800
Subject: Rights routing & training exclusion — MSA/Order Form redlines

Diego,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached are Novasys's initial redlines to the MSA and the Order Form (attached: Novasys_MSA_redline_20290111.pdf and OrderForm_v3_track_changes.docx). High level asks:

- We need explicit assignment/clear license for "Outputs" that Novasys will productize (we call these "Product Content") so our downstream teams can ship without ambiguity.
- We will not provide a blanket opt-in for training. Novasys requires that customer data and Product Content be excluded from model training unless Novasys expressly opts in via the Order Form.
- For feedback/telemetry, we can provide a limited, nonexclusive feedback license for improvement of services, but not for training core foundational models.
- We propose definitions and an exhibit that carve out Product Content and sample attributions.

Please confirm who from Redwood legal/product should take primary ownership of the redline exchange. Tom and I are on a tight procurement timeline and would like to get to an agreed text quickly. We can also do a 30-minute call if it helps.

Best,
Elise Moreno
Director, Procurement & Partnerships
Novasys

Attachments: Novasys_MSA_redline_20290111.pdf (PDF redline summary), OrderForm_v3_track_changes.docx (Order form with inline changes)
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Elise Moreno <elise.moreno@novasys.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-01-12 11:02 -08:00
Subject: Re: Rights routing & training exclusion — MSA/Order Form redlines

Elise — thanks, received. We appreciate the clarity on Product Content and the timeline. High-level response before we get legal into the redlines:

- Redwood's default stance is to grant customers broad rights to Outputs for their internal use and productization via a license rather than assignment of title to model-derived artifacts. Assignment of output ownership is unusual for our platform; can you explain the downstream constraints driving the request? (e.g., regulatory filing, resale, or exclusive commercial packaging?)
- We can accommodate an explicit training exclusion for customer-provided data and Product Content; we typically implement that as an opt-out in the Order Form with the vendor withholding rights to use excluded data for model training unless the customer checks the opt-in box.
- For feedback/telemetry we propose a narrowly scoped nonexclusive license limited to service improvements and aggregated performance analytics; no right to include identifiable Product Content in model training.

I've looped in Ben (legal), Laura (product), and Monica (CS/ops) to help turn these high-level positions into concrete redline language. Ben — can you take the MSA doc and draft two options we can present to Novasys: (A) License-first approach with explicit Product Content carveout, (B) Limited title-assignment for "Product Content" only, with contractual guarantees and indemnities?

If Novasys can share specific examples of what they consider "productized outputs" that would help us draft precise definitions. Also suggest a 30-min working session tomorrow afternoon; Elise, do you have a slot?

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-01-12 15:30 -08:00
Subject: Re: Rights routing & training exclusion — MSA/Order Form redlines

Diego — taking this on. I reviewed Novasys's PDF and Order Form. Attached I'm sending a working draft (OrderForm_v3_redlines_BC.docx) with two paths: license-based and narrow-assignment-based language. Key suggestions below.

1) Outputs vs Product Content: define "Outputs" broadly (responses generated by the Service). Define "Product Content" narrowly as Outputs that are modified, curated, and shipped by Novasys as part of a commercial offering, with examples (e.g., automated reports bundled with Novasys UI). If we go assignment route, limit it to Product Content only and require a clear handback/evidence process.

2) Training exclusion: clause to read — "Customer Data and Product Content shall not be used to train or improve any Model or foundation model used by Redwood, except where Customer provides explicit written consent on a per-order or per-dataset basis." This is workable; we'll add Auditability and a technical implementation note (separate SOW if needed).

3) Feedback License: propose "Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, royalty-free, worldwide license to use anonymized, aggregated feedback data to improve the Service, provided such feedback does not contain Customer Data or Product Content as defined herein."

4) Liability/Indemnity: if we accept assignment of Product Content title, require carveouts for third-party IP claims and a rep/indemnity bucket; otherwise maintain standard warranty & indemnity structure.

I recommend we present both paths to Novasys with a short pros/cons list. Laura/Monica — can you each add a short note about operational impact (SLA/ops for enforcement, tagging/dataflows) and product risk?

Ben
Associate General Counsel
Redwood Inference

Attachments mentioned: OrderForm_v3_redlines_BC.docx (legal working draft)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-01-13 09:46 -08:00
Subject: Re: Rights routing & training exclusion — MSA/Order Form redlines (product/ops notes)

Adding product/ops context — copied into the thread for Novasys visibility.

- If we allow Novasys to productize Outputs with assignment or a broad license, we need clear telemetry and retention controls. Ops will need a guaranteed tag/metadata flag at request time to mark Product Content vs ephemeral Outputs so we can enforce training exclusion and retention windows.
- Implementation complexity: per-customer opt-outs for training require runtime flags and downstream model pipelines to honor exclusions. That's doable but increases per-deal operational overhead (audit logs, testing). If we agree to assignment for Product Content, we need a playbook: how will customers provide evidence of productization? We should include a short exhibit listing acceptable evidence (e.g., product screenshots, SKU IDs).

- SLOs: productized outputs may be subject to stricter availability and support SLAs; may require dedicated routing or higher-tier support. This has commercial implications for Diego/AE.

I suggest we propose two practical guardrails in the Order Form: 1) Product Content definition/examples; 2) Operational exhibit for training-exclusion handling (required metadata and contact point). If Novasys accepts those, engineering involvement will be limited to building the flag and audit hooks.

Laura
Head of Product
Redwood Inference
From: Elise Moreno <elise.moreno@novasys.io>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Becker <t.becker@novasys.io>, Novasys Legal <legal@novasys.io>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-01-14 10:12 -08:00
Subject: Re: Rights routing & training exclusion — MSA/Order Form redlines

Thanks Diego, Ben, Laura — useful start. Novasys's procurement constraints are: our licensing team needs explicit assignment or an exclusive-like right for Product Content that will be embedded into our SaaS product; without assignment we cannot allow downstream resale or sublicensing by a third-party without additional clearance. Examples of Product Content: system-generated data bundles we package into our SaaS insights module, or UI-ready narrative responses that we include as core features.

We are open to the two-path approach. A couple of clarifying asks:
- If Redwood will not assign title, can you provide a heavily-scoped, perpetual license allowing Novasys to distribute Product Content to Novasys customers, sublicense for resale, and make derivative works? We need sublicense rights.
- On the training exclusion: Novasys will not opt-in by default. We require that the Order Form clearly state that Customer Data and Product Content are excluded from training unless Customer checks an affirmative opt-in.

Attached is a marked-up MSA excerpt where we added a Product Content exhibit and sample language for assignment/license options (attached: Novasys_MSA_redline_20290111.pdf). We need to move quickly — procurement is aiming to complete legal by the end of next week. Can Redwood's legal either accept one of the two paths or provide a final counter by EOD 2029-01-17?

Regards,
Elise Moreno
Director, Procurement & Partnerships
Novasys
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Elise Moreno <elise.moreno@novasys.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-01-17 08:03 -08:00
Subject: Re: Rights routing & training exclusion — MSA/Order Form redlines

Elise, team — thanks for the prompt turnaround and the exhibit. Summarizing a pragmatic path we can present as Redwood's counter:

1) Default: Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, transferable, non-exclusive license to use Outputs and to distribute or sublicense Outputs that Customer has expressly designated as "Product Content" in the Order Form. This license covers reproduction, distribution, modification and creation of derivative works by Customer.

2) Optional Assignment: For Product Content only, Redwood can agree to assignment of title on a limited basis if Customer meets the following conditions: (i) Product Content is identified via the exhibit and evidence process; (ii) Customer accepts specific reps/indemnities for third-party claims arising from Product Content; (iii) Customer agrees to a separate escrow/archival evidence workflow. Assignment will be limited to Product Content as defined.

3) Training Exclusion: Customer Data and Product Content shall not be used to train or improve Redwood's foundation models or third-party foundation models unless Customer gives an affirmative opt-in in the Order Form. Redwood may use anonymized, aggregated telemetry (explicitly excluding Customer Data and Product Content) to improve service operations and performance.

4) Feedback License: Redwood requests a narrow, nonexclusive license to use anonymized, aggregated feedback for service improvement; explicit exclusion of Product Content and Customer Data.

Operational commitments: Laura/Monica will provide an exhibit that defines Product Content examples and the evidence checklist; our engineering/ops team will scope the minimal metadata tagging and audit hooks required for enforcement. Commercial: we recognize that assignment or broad sublicense rights often require different pricing or an enterprise add-on.

Next steps: Ben will translate the bullets above into a single tracked draft for the MSA/Order Form. Diego proposes we aim to exchange that draft with Novasys Legal by 2029-01-18 and target final signoff by 2029-01-22. Elise — does that timeline work for you?

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
